newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on Pakistan buy, corn surge.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on Pakistan buy, corn surge.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on news Pakistan bought 450,000 tonnes of wheat from the U.S. and on a fund-generated surge to near limit gains in the corn pit, traders said.

"The early gains in corn off the cattle numbers took us into buy stops that rallied the whole floor," said Mark Cermak of Chicago trade house O'Connor and Co. "They were short over 80 million bushels (corn) and may be net long after today."
There had been speculation late last week that Pakistan would purchase the wheat from the U.S. rather than from Australia because Australia is booked up for the near term.
The talk was confirmed on Monday when a Pakistan Food and Agriculture Ministry official announced the purchase.
Traders also said wheat was oversold and due for a bounce with evidence last week of a large number of fund shorts in wheat adding credence to that scenario.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders data Friday showed non commercials as of last Tuesday were short wheat by roughly 86.3 million bushels and long by 31.4 million bushels.
Wheat closed two to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-3/4 at $3.64-1/4.
USDA's wheat export inspections total at 13.442 million bushels compared with expectations for 10.0 million to 14.0 million.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, above the 9,092 traded Friday.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, above the 1,551 traded Friday.
